Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior

Class EyeInfluence

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.EyeInfluence
public final class EyeInfluence extends Object
What a single active EyeBehavior exerts on one eye for one simulation tick (not one frame). This is how behaviors participate in the physics model instead of overwriting it in the renderer: the pupil is a point-mass, and a behavior that wants to move it contributes a spring — an anchor point in the eye's unit disk plus a stiffness — that the simulator adds to the ordinary forces (gravity, socket pseudo-forces). When the stiffness fades at the end of the effect, gravity naturally takes the pupil back down; there is no blend and no separate hidden simulation to snap to.
  • anchorX/anchorY + stiffness — the pupil spring. stiffness == 0 means the behavior doesn't drive the pupil at all (it keeps wobbling freely): grow, blink, and color leave it there. Stare anchors at center, side/cross anchor off to one side, swirl's anchor orbits.
  • eyeScaleMul — multiplies the eye's configured scale (grow). Non-physical overlay.
  • squashY — multiplies the eye's vertical scale (blink). Non-physical overlay.
  • corneaTint / tintAmount — lerp the cornea toward corneaTint by tintAmount (color-change). Non-physical overlay.

Reused per eye: the simulator calls reset() before asking the active behavior to fill it, so an eye with no active behavior keeps the neutral defaults below (pure physics, no overlays).
